slides.title: Documentation
points: Change management is not complete when the technical work ends.
Diagrams, policies, procedures, and version history must stay synchronized with the real environment.

slides.title: Updating Diagrams
slides.teach: Diagrams should be updated when architecture, devices, connections, trust boundaries, data flows, or other documented relationships change.

course.learn: Diagrams should be updated when architecture, devices, connections, trust boundaries, data flows, or other documented relationships change.

breakdown.explanation: The picture of the environment should match the real environment.
Network diagrams, data-flow diagrams, architecture diagrams, rack diagrams, trust-boundary diagrams.

course.why: Outdated diagrams can mislead administrators, auditors, and incident responders about what actually exists or how systems connect.
course.example: A new firewall and network segment are added, so the network diagram is revised to show the new path and security boundary.
course.exam: Scenario clue: topology, architecture, devices, or data flows changed → UPDATE DIAGRAMS.
course.check_q: A new network segment and firewall are added to production. Which documentation should be updated to reflect the new topology?

slides.title: Updating Policies / Procedures
slides.teach: Policies and procedures should be updated when approved requirements, responsibilities, workflows, or operational practices change.

course.learn: Policies and procedures should be updated when approved requirements, responsibilities, workflows, or operational practices change.

breakdown.explanation: Written rules and instructions should describe what the organization actually requires and does.
Authentication policy, incident-response procedure, patching procedure, access-control procedure.

course.why: Outdated policies and procedures create inconsistent behavior, compliance problems, and confusion about the approved process.
course.example: The organization requires MFA for administrators, so the authentication policy and account-provisioning procedure are updated to include the new requirement.
course.exam: Scenario clue: rules, requirements, or approved operating steps changed → UPDATE POLICIES/PROCEDURES.
course.check_q: A company begins requiring MFA for all administrators. Which documentation should be revised to reflect the requirement?

slides.title: Version Control
slides.teach: Version control tracks revisions so teams can identify what changed, who changed it, when it changed, and—when supported—restore an earlier version.

course.learn: Version control tracks revisions so teams can identify what changed, who changed it, when it changed, and—when supported—restore an earlier version.

breakdown.explanation: It provides a history of changes to documents, code, configurations, or other controlled content.
Git history, document revision history, configuration versions, policy revision numbers.

course.why: Version control improves traceability, accountability, collaboration, and recovery from unwanted changes.
course.example: A security team compares the current firewall configuration with last week's version to determine what was modified and by whom.
course.exam: Scenario clue: revision history, previous version, who changed it, or what changed → VERSION CONTROL.
course.check_q: A team needs to determine what changed in a configuration, who changed it, and recover the previous revision. Which concept is most relevant?

blocks.title: Documentation shortcuts
rows: Topology, architecture, devices, connections, data flows
Requirements, rules, responsibilities, or operating steps
Revisions to documents, code, or configurations

blocks.title: What kind of information became outdated?
items: If the actual topology, architecture, connections, or data flows changed, the diagram should be revised.
Example: A new firewall and subnet are added, so the network diagram must show them.
Rules or process changed → Update policies/procedures
If the organization changes a requirement or approved workflow, its written policy or procedure should match.
Example: MFA becomes mandatory for administrators, so authentication documentation is revised.
If the question asks what changed, who changed it, when it changed, or how to recover an earlier revision, think version control.
Example: The team compares today's firewall configuration with last week's version.
blocks.example: Fast memory: Diagram = environment · Policy/Procedure = rules and steps · Version Control = revision history

questions.q: A company adds a new firewall and network segment. Which documentation should be updated to show the changed topology?
questions.explanation: Diagrams should be updated when architecture, connections, or network topology changes.

questions.q: An organization begins requiring MFA for all administrators. Which documentation should be revised to reflect the new requirement and operating steps?
questions.explanation: Policies and procedures should reflect current approved requirements and processes.

questions.q: A security team needs to see what changed in a configuration, who changed it, and restore an earlier revision. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Version control tracks revisions and supports traceability and rollback to earlier versions.

questions.q: Incident responders rely on an old network diagram and initially investigate the wrong traffic path. What change-management practice was most likely missed?
questions.explanation: The diagram should have been updated when the environment changed.
